routes.description: Establish that unexplained nonmaximal parameters are arbitrary, that fundamental reality has perfection-relevant positive attributes, and that eliminating or explaining their limits supports a perfect or quasi-perfect foundation.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if arbitrariness supplies a warranted demand for explanation, foundational greatness is supported, explanations do not merely relocate arbitrary limits, and the resulting absence of arbitrary boundaries yields substantively God-like perfection.

motionBridge.description: Connect the absence of arbitrary limits in foundational power, positivity, and persistence to a perfect or quasi-perfect reality with substantively God-like attributes.

centralBridges.description: Establish that an unexplained nonmaximal degree among rationally available alternatives calls for explanation and counts against treating that degree as fundamental.
Supply a basis for attributing positive value or greatness to fundamental reality, including through mentality, valuable capacities, or value-entailing grounds.
Show that a necessitating explanation of a limited outcome cannot remove the problem merely by relocating the same arbitrary selectivity into its ground.
Show that explaining limits as far as possible supports maximal or quasi-maximal perfection-relevant attributes rather than an explained but nonmaximal stopping point.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Specify how the limits principle can guide comparison among worldviews even when independent commitments make its application defeasible.
Distinguish necessitating metaphysical grounding from indeterministic creative explanation when determining whether arbitrariness transfers to an explanatory source.

routes.description: Show that arbitrary-limits reasoning remains dependent on contestable explanatory principles and supplementary assumptions, while non-theistic foundations can contain explained limits or offset their costs through broader theoretical virtues.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if the limits principle lacks theory-neutral support, foundational greatness or mentality remains unestablished, or an explained nonmaximal foundation remains possible, preventing the argument itself from reaching God-like perfection.

motionBridge.description: Demonstrate that the limits argument does not by itself warrant the transition from a fundamental reality to a minded, maximally great, God-like foundation.

centralBridges.description: Establish that any cost from unexplained limits must be assessed alongside the simplicity, explanatory power, and other virtues of competing total theories.
Show that track-record, intuition, and relevant-difference support for explaining limits is defeasible or equally supports rival principles absent a symmetry breaker.
Show that a mindless foundation may be axiologically neutral and that producing or enabling value does not by itself confer value or greatness on its ground.
Preserve the possibility that metaphysical necessity, essence, or a deeper property explains a nonmaximal degree without making that degree arbitrary.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Require a stable distinction among unexplainedness, inexplicability, conceivable alternatives, and comparative non-difference in the operative account of arbitrariness.
Test whether proposed deeper explanations of divine structural limits remain compatible with the theological commitments the argument is intended to support.

sections.title: Arbitrariness and the Demand for Explanation
sections.rationale: This issue fixes the meaning of an arbitrary limit and determines whether apparently irrelevant nonmaximal parameters generate a defensible explanatory demand at the fundamental level.

sections.title: Defeasible Principles and Whole-Theory Comparison
sections.rationale: This issue determines whether the limits principle has theory-neutral force, remains one comparative consideration among many, or requires a symmetry breaker against rival explanatory generalizations.

sections.title: Foundational Value, Greatness, and Mentality
sections.rationale: The route toward perfection requires fundamental reality to possess some perfection-relevant value or greatness, making the grounding, productive-capacity, and mentality bridges indispensable.

sections.title: Explained Submaximality and Arbitrariness Inheritance
sections.rationale: This issue governs whether necessity, essence, or deeper grounds can explain a nonmaximal limit, and whether such explanations remove arbitrariness or merely relocate it.

sections.title: From Reduced Arbitrariness to God-Like Perfection
sections.rationale: This issue identifies the motion-level completion condition: whether reducing unexplained boundaries yields maximal power, positivity, and persistence, a quasi-perfect foundation, or only a limited comparative constraint.
